descriptor: Family bakery feeding Marrow Bridge since 1998

voice.summary: Speaks like the baker leaning on the counter at seven in the morning: plain, kind and a little proud of the crust. Sentences are short and sensory, and the street always comes before the brand.
dos: Name the real things: flour, doorsteps, the four o'clock start
Use we and our, and say neighbour instead of customer
Keep sentences short enough to say with flour on your hands
donts: Corporate phrases like artisan experience or premium offering
Talking about scale when the story is one oven and one street

taglines: We bake for the street we live on
Up at four, open at seven
Every loaf ends on a doorstep
boilerplate: Kettlewood Bakehouse is a family bakery in Marrow Bridge that has made slow-risen loaves, honest pastries and the occasional too-warm cinnamon bun since 1998.

microcopy.success: Thanks, we will save you a loaf
microcopy.error: The oven door stuck. Try that again?
microcopy.empty: No loaves left on this shelf yet

logo.note: A sprouting grain stem nods to local flour and the slow rise of the dough.
